phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: Periods of winter inactivity from November to March (Wikipedia, Pacific gopher snake). The NPS says the snakes overwinter without feeding in colder climates but gives no months.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: NPS: 'mate in spring'. Months are authored from that wording. Wikipedia (Pacific gopher snake) instead gives males competing to mate from June to August; the two sources conflict and the record follows the NPS.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: NPS: 'laying 3-9 eggs in early summer'. Months are authored from that wording.

phases.name: young
phases.note: NPS and Wikipedia (Pacific gopher snake): eggs hatch 2 to 2.5 months after laying, so hatchlings appear from late summer into autumn.

taxonomy.note: Authority (Blainville, 1835) and the accepted name from GBIF usage key 2453826 and ITIS TSN 209400. GBIF's backbone gives class Squamata with no order for this species; the conventional classification (class Reptilia, order Squamata, family Colubridae) is used instead, as the amniote database gives it.

external.note: GBIF usage key 2453826, iNaturalist taxon 29044 (checked live on 2026-10-31: species rank, active, name Pituophis catenifer), ITIS TSN 209400 (checked by name search on 2026-10-31), Wikidata Q2705737 (taxon name Pituophis catenifer, rank species; its GBIF, iNaturalist and ITIS identifiers agree with these). Wikidata's English label reads 'Pacific gopher snake'; the record uses 'gopher snake' from the Wikipedia article title.

common_names.note: English name from the Wikipedia article title for Pituophis catenifer. Only English is given; no French or German label was verified.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005); the English Wikipedia article gives 'Least Concern' (IUCN 3.1).

range.note: Country-level only. The Wikipedia article says the species is 'endemic to North America' and that subspecies span 'southern Canada, the continental United States, and Mexico', which gives CA, US and MX. No introduced population is mentioned. Subnational native status is not recorded in this version.

traits.limb_count.note: Snakes have no walking limbs; limb_count 0 is the schema's convention for a limbless animal. No openly licensed source was fetched that states this directly.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Slither is the snake's only locomotion mode in the record. The NPS and Wikipedia describe no swimming or climbing mode that is needed here: Wikipedia says the snake may swim in small bodies of water to cool down, which is not a locomotion mode for this record, so Swim is omitted. Climb is not sourced and is omitted.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Squamate reptile, ectothermic. The Pacific gopher snake article says the snake 'seeks cooler spots' when temperatures heat up beyond its tolerance, which is consistent with ectothermy. Ectothermy is a reptile-wide trait applied here; no gopher-specific quote was fetched.

traits.skin.note: Snake skin is covered in scales (reptile-wide trait); no gopher-specific quote was fetched.

traits.perching.note: Authored as false. Gopher snakes climb poorly if at all; climbing is not sourced in this record, and the perching behaviour is not modelled.

traits.mass_kg.note: Amniote database adult_body_mass_g = 7275.5 g, converted to kg and rounded to 7.28 kg. The database value is a single species-level figure; no mass range was found in an open source, so mass_range_kg is omitted.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia gives adult total length as '36-84 in (91-213 cm)'; the NPS gives 2.5-7 feet (76-213 cm). 1.52 m is the midpoint of the Wikipedia range (91 and 213 cm), a derived range midpoint rather than a measured mean.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia: 'Wild gopher snakes typically live 12 to 15 years.' The midpoint, 13.5, is derived. The oldest captive individual (over 33 years) is a different statistic and is not used. Amniote longevity_y 15.8 is not used because it is not documented as a wild typical value.

traits.diet.note: NPS: 'Diet varies according to size, ranging from insects to rodents, lizards, and birds and their eggs.' Wikipedia (Pacific gopher snake): 'mainly consists of small rodents' plus birds, bird eggs and lizards, and 'occasionally insects or bats'. The 0.95 vertebrate / 0.05 invertebrate split is authored from these statements; no percentage was published in the sources.

traits.social.note: Authored as solitary: the sources fetched for this record describe no social grouping. Communal nesting or hibernation is not represented here.

traits.activity_pattern.note: NPS: 'It is usually diurnal, but can be active at night in warm weather.' Wikipedia (Pacific gopher snake): 'mainly diurnal'. Warm-weather night activity is documented but not modelled by the behaviour program; the record is Diurnal.

traits.defense.note: The documented response is threat display: 'inflate its body, flatten its head, and vigorously shake its tail'; it hisses and may strike with a closed mouth. The schema has no display category, so Flee is the closest enum value and is used for the behaviour program's flee action. This is a limitation of the schema.

traits.wariness.note: Authored judgement (0.5). No source gives a wariness scale.

habitat.use.note: Predominantly ground-dwelling. NPS: 'enters rodent burrows in search of prey'; Wikipedia: shelters in 'burrows, leaf litter, shade, under rocks'. ground 0.8 and fossorial 0.2 are authored shares.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Shelters in burrows (Wikipedia: 'burrows, leaf litter, shade, under rocks'; NPS: enters rodent burrows).

habitat.resources.note: small_vertebrate and invertebrate predation weights follow the authored diet split. burrow (1.0), leaf_litter (0.4) and shelter (0.5) cover the sheltering statements; the 'shelter' tag stands in for 'under rocks' and 'shade', which have no specific resource tag. All weights are authored.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia: prefers 'drier habitats such as meadows, fields and agricultural farmlands'. urban_affinity Adapter is authored judgement; no source addresses urban use.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: 'periods of inactivity in the winter from November to March'. Brumation is the closest enum value; the source does not establish a reptile-wide brumation or hibernation mechanism for this species.

seasonal.triggers.note: Authored temperature thresholds (enter below 10 C for five days, leave above 10 C for five days). No open source gives thresholds for this species.

seasonal.phases.note: Winter inactivity Nov-Mar (Wikipedia). Spring mating and early-summer laying (NPS, with months authored); the Wikipedia June-August mating window conflicts and is recorded in the phase note. Hatching 2 to 2.5 months after laying (NPS, Wikipedia; amniote incubation_d 60 days). Phase months are authored from these statements.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Oviparous (egg-laying, from the NPS). Egg stage duration 60 days from amniote incubation_d. No juvenile duration is given in an open source, so no Juvenile stage is recorded.

look.note: Authored judgement: serpentine body plan, tan body with brown dorsal blotches and a cream belly, from general descriptions of the species' pattern; no colour values were taken from a source.

behavior.note: Species-local program fsm-gopher-snake-v1 (behavior.json). Flee and calm distances, food distance and night thresholds are authored judgement values, not measurements. The program has no drink state and no basking gait fixed to a source.

vocalizations.note: HONEST GAP: the NPS says the gopher snake 'can hiss loudly when agitated'. The vocalization schema requires a cooldown_s value, and no source gives one, so no vocalization is recorded and the list is empty.
